reviews.title: Customizable and Intuitive, With Room to Grow on AI and Theming
reviews.text: The customization is what keeps me coming back. Being able to shape a page into exactly what I need, instead of working inside someone else's template, means I've been able to build out little systems that work almost like mini apps for different parts of my workflow. That flexibility alone has sped up how quickly I can set something new up when a project needs it. It's also just more intuitive than I expected going in. I came from Asana, which handles basic task tracking fine but gets rigid fast once your needs grow past that. Notion has a gentler learning curve even though it can do a lot more, so I didn't have to fight the tool to get it to work the way I think. Having docs, databases, and tracking all live in one place has cut down on a lot of the manual copying and tab switching I used to deal with, which adds up to real time saved over a normal week. My biggest gripe is how limited the customization is when it comes to look and feel. You can build incredibly complex structures but you're stuck with the same handful of colors and themes, which feels backwards for a tool that's supposed to be flexible. I also wish pinning worked better with scrolling, on longer pages I lose my spot constantly and end up scrolling back up to find a section I was just looking at. Performance is another thing. It's fine for smaller stuff, but once a workspace gets big, lots of linked databases, nested views, that kind of thing, pages start to lag and it's noticeable. Not a dealbreaker, just annoying when I'm trying to move fast. The AI features are also just okay. Good for a quick summary or cleaning something up, but it doesn't feel like it actually knows my workspace, more bolted on than built in.

reviews.title: We use Notion for basically everything…
reviews.text: We use Notion for basically everything - our agency KB, project management, and CRM. It’s the backbone of how we stay organized. The Good Stuff: The customizability is unmatched. We’re very API-forward, so the way it integrates with Make and the MCP we use with Claude is a total game-changer for our automation. In the last year, Notion has been pumping out updates so fast I can’t even catch up. I’m positive I’m missing out on half the new features, but here are the ones actually moving the needle for us: AI Meeting Recording: This is huge. Since it’s local and you don’t have to have a "bot" join the call, it’s way less intrusive. Plus, because it runs locally, I can use it for phone calls and in-person meetings, which is a massive plus. Database Upgrades: Love the recent additions like conditional coloring; it makes scanning high-level data so much easier. Notion Calendar: The recent UI updates have made this a staple in my daily workflow. The Not-So-Good Stuff: Notion Mail: Honestly, it needs some love. The sorting and AI features leave a lot to be desired, and it bugs out on me pretty often. It’s a great concept, but it's not quite "there" yet. The Learning Curve: There is definitely a steep curve for new users. I really wish there was a better way to introduce basic features to new team members without it feeling overwhelming. My Wishlist: Notion Chat: I’d love a native chat feature similar to Slack so we could finally keep the "talk" where the "work" is. Basic Text Formatting: I’d love to use Notion as a legitimate word processor (like to write a book), but it’s missing the basics. You can't do double line spacing and you can't even do paragraph indents. Overall, it’s an incredible tool that we couldn't run the agency without, even if I'm constantly chasing the latest update.

Despite acknowledging that the subscription was unused, Notion refused to issue any refund, stating that their policy only allows refunds if contacted within three days of invoice creation. No exception was considered, even though the service was not used at all and I contacted them immediately upon discovering the charges. While I understand that companies have internal policies, I find it unreasonable and unfair to completely deny refunds in cases where no service was consumed and the customer acts promptly once aware of the billing.
